 Indiana Pacers Indiana finished their opening week of the season with a 2-2 record and had some unfortunate injuries along the way. Week two was doubly worse as they went winless in four matchups and added even more players to the injury report. 
--> Indiana finished their opening week of the season with a 2-2 record and had some unfortunate injuries along the way. Week two was doubly worse as they went winless in four matchups and added even more players to the injury report. 
 Before their nationally televised game against LeBron James and the Phialdelphia 76ers, the Pacers announced that Tyrese Haliburton had a hamstring strain and would be out at least two weeks. His status moving forward would be week-to-week as it was a mild strain. 
--> Before their nationally televised game against LeBron James and the Phialdelphia 76ers, the Pacers announced that Tyrese Haliburton had a hamstring strain and would be out at least two weeks. His status moving forward would be week-to-week as it was a mild strain. 
 Coach Carlisle shared that Ben Sheppard had successful surgery to repair a torn meniscus and later clarified on his weekly radio segment that he was unsure if Sheppard would return this season.

 The Pacers rallied together for a gritty effort against the 76ers, but unfortuantely fell short as they could not cotain Tyrese Maxey who dropped 17 of Philly's 39 fourth-quarter points. They lost this battle 114-109, but the effort was there and it looked like there would be momentum to build upon.

Mandatory Credit: Isabella Frias-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They traveled to Miami for their next game and no new players were listed on the injury report. Unfortuantely, Obi Toppin had a weird back issue that flared up during the team's walkthrough on Friday and it caused him to miss the game. The Heat were at full strength and destroyed the Pacers front court with Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo leading the way. It was a 145-125 blowout.

 Hoping to snap a three-game losing streak, the Pacers hosted the winless Brooklyn Nets on Sunday evening. Indiana's high-powered offensive game against Miami was left in South Beach as the Pacers and Nets had a rock fight. The Nets pulled out a 98-90 victory with both teams struggling to throw the ball into the ocean all night. The good news was that no new players were added to the injury report, but Toppin remained out.

 Then on Monday evening the ' Pacers ' took on the Hawks. The injury report that looked so clean was now chalk full of them. Before the pregame press conferences, Carlisle shared that only seven players would play, but 10 guys would be out. Then moments before tipoff, Kelly Oubre Jr. --one of the original seven healthy players-- hurt his knee and the Pacers were down to just 6 players: three standard roster guys (Huff, Jackson and Walker) and three two-way guys (Brown, Smith and Slawson). The "Super Six" poured their blood, sweat and tears into the game, but fell short 108-104 in an unforgettable effort.

 Oct 28, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Philadelphia 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey (0) dribbles the ball while Indiana Pacers guard Braden Smith (3) defends in the first half at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Super Six 
Heart. Grit. Tenacity. Effort. Togetherness. Unselfish. 
It was uplifting watching these six players battle their tails off for the entirety of a 48-minute game while their top-8 -players were on the sideline in street clothes. 
This group of six proved that if you compete at a high level you give yourself a chance to win any game. Guys have been battling injuries left and right, but the spirit that these six played with has been lacking all season. Hopefully the Pacers key players used Monday night as an example of how they can get better and get this team back on track.

 Braden Smith 
 The rookie point guard got his first career start against the Atlanta Hawks . In 42-minutes of play, he recorded a double-double: 19 points and 10 assists. He shot 8-13 from the field, had 2 steals and looked like he belonged. With a shorthanded roster, the rookie took advantage of an opportunity and showed fans why the team targeted him as a target in the draft.

 Andrew Nembhard 
In three games, Nembhard led the team in scoring. He averaged 21 points per game, but his shooting percentage was a woeful 39.2%. He did however connect on 40% from three and made 86% of his free throws. He led the team in minutes per game with 33.5.

Without Tyrese Haliburton this team has struggled offensively. Indiana was 3rd in assists last week, and fell all the way to 21st. If that isn't a sign of how imporrant Haliburton is to the offense, I don't know what is. Indiana needs much better ball movement from the guys on the floor...and they need to hit their shots. Too many potential assists left on the board.

 Pascal Siakam's Shooting 
Last week was a terrific week of efficiency for Siakam, but without Haliburton and the defenses attention more fixated on him, he struggeld from the field. Indiana finished the week with the 7th worst offense, the 10th worst defense and the 8th worst net rating. 
When you lose several games, get blown out by 20 in one, and struggle to score the basketball in 2 of them, these numbers are likely to happen, This is clearly a reflectio of their injury problems and a reminder how much Tyrese Haliburton means to the success of this team.

 Three-Point Shooting 
The Pacers are the 8th worst three-point shooting team during this stretch making just 32.9%. While it is actually 0.2% better than last week, they dropped from 16th in the NBA to 23rd. The Pacers starting front court during this stretch of games is Pascal Siakam, Aaron Nesmith and Jay Huff. They combined to go 8-41 (19.5%) from long-distance.

 Injuries 
I listed injuries as an ugly last week and there has been no improvement on this front. The Pacers health issues are a real concern and Carlisle said that the team will not bring players back before they are ready. Haliburton will be out at least another week, Sheppard is going to be out for a significant amount of time, and Furphy is nowhere close to returning. 
On the positive side of things, Zubac was seen sitting on the bench against the Hawks for the first time since the Pacers-Bucks game and is questionable for the Grizzlies game. Toppin appears to be getting closer to a return. McConnell did some injury rehab work by practicing with the Noblesville Boom, and Oubre's knee injury didn't seem too serious. 
Until this roster gets fully restored, it will be an uphill battle to win games. But things are pointing to the team getting closer to fully healthy versus not, even if it means they're without Haliburton for an extended amount of time.
